headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Superset can expose shared analytics outputs while the prompt-list agent can be treated as trusted content, but no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-prompts and Superset. awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository with no runnable I/O surfaces, while Superset only exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. Without a bridge, prompt injection via one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies prompt text from awesome-prompts into Superset dashboards or SQL editors, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two, re-evaluate for prompt injection.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted prompt content into operational fields.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to any shared content channel.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization for imported prompt text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts touches no data classes and has no network egress, while Superset has allowlisted egress and a Superset API. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or sensitive data, so leakage is limited; however, if the pair is co-located, Superset could transmit whatever content it receives from the prompt repository or operator.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace or repository, content copied from awesome-prompts can flow into Superset.
IF Superset is configured to query external services with imported content, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Superset and the prompt repository in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets or regulated data in any shared workspace.
Review allowlisted egress destinations in Superset.
requires-engineering: enforce per-project storage isolation.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks before outbound API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable and requests no privileges, while Superset is a data-engineering app with API access and allowlisted egress. There is no documented overlapping write surface, so direct conflict is unlikely; uncertainty remains because the profiles are unverified and do not fully describe deployment state, so the safer low rating is chosen.
conditions: IF both are deployed against the same mutable backend or filesystem, write conflicts can occur.
IF Superset is granted additional write scopes outside the profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep deployments read-only where possible.
Separate mutable resources by project.
Check Superset API permissions before enabling writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared backends.
requires-engineering: add per-agent namespace isolation.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt content that Superset users may treat as authoritative guidance, and Superset can act on that content through its API and analytics workflows. No verification step is documented, so mistaken instructions or bad prompts can cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Superset users import prompts from awesome-prompts as operational instructions, errors can propagate.
IF Superset automations consume prompt-derived text without review, cascading mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Require human review before using imported prompts.
Label prompt-library content as non-authoritative.
Test any prompt-derived workflow in a staging Superset instance.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before API-triggered actions.
requires-engineering: log provenance for imported instructions.

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles show no data classes touched, no secrets handled, and no residency or retention mismatch. awesome-prompts is a prompt repository and Superset is an analytics tool, but the evidence does not show regulated data flowing between them, so no compliance breach is established.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance must be reassessed.
IF Superset is connected to a regulated dataset or external tenant, residency and retention controls must be checked.
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data is present in the current workflow.
Review Superset retention settings.
Keep prompt-library content free of personal data.
requires-engineering: document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
